title: Incremental release attenuation and traffic signalization for safe upgrades
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: design and implement a general-purpose "signalization and attenuation" system to control incremental traffic ramps during upgrades. This ticket covers the policy model, runtime hooks for applying coarse- and fine-grained attenuation, automatic rollback triggers, feature-flag integration, and the compatibility rules for LTS channels and pinned versions.

Motivation: existing progressive delivery tooling at Redwood relies on static ramp schedules and manual monitoring; recent incidents showed that sudden downstream latency spikes can cascade across cohorts. We need an automated attenuation layer that senses multiple 'signals' (errors, p95 latency, model quality regressions) and reduces ramp velocity or performs safe fallback.

Scope:
- Policy DSL for signal thresholds, weighting, and decay curves (stored in git as YAML)
- Runtime enforcement in the control plane: cohort assignment, fractional weights, ramp timers, and attenuation operations (slow-down, pause, reverse)
- Health signals to monitor: 5xx error rate, p50/p95 latency, token drop anomalies, model-level regression metrics (eval set DPR), and customer-reported rate from support channels
- Automatic rollback policy: multi-signal consensus + staged fallback to compatible model variant or prior LTS build
- Feature-flagged rollout path to allow A/B experiments without overriding LTS pins
- Integration with Console: visual traffic curve, manual override, audit log entries, and per-tenant policy evaluation results
- Runbooks and chaos test harness for exercising attenuation and rollback in staging and pre-prod

Non-goals: full rewrite of canary workflow; this augments existing canary/cohort systems with signal-aware modulation.
acceptance_criteria: Signal DSL defined and stored in repo with examples for linear ramp, exponential decay, and hold-on-failure
Control plane implements attenuation primitives (slow, hold, reverse) and exposes an evaluation API
Automatic rollback triggers work end-to-end in staging: i.e., simulated p95 spike triggers attenuation then rollback to previous variant
Console UI surfaces live signal scores and allows manual override with audit trail
Security review completed and KMS keys verified for audit log retention

comments: 2025-02-11 — Asha: Kickoff meeting; agreed to model policies as declarative YAML checked into infra repo. Primary signals: error_rate_5xx, latency_p95, eval_regression_score.
2025-02-18 — Luca: Prototype attenuation engine added to control-plane (branch: feature/attenuation-proto). It supports slow/hold/reverse and per-cohort timers. Needs tests and telemetry hooks.

2025-02-24 — Priya: Telemetry scorer implemented; uses sliding-window anomaly detector. Initial thresholds are conservative (error_rate>0.5%, p95>2s). Observed a false-positive with synthetic test; tuning required.

2025-02-28 — Nia: Console mockups reviewed in design critique. CTA for manual override will include 'pause ramp', 'resume ramp', and 'force rollback'. Audit events will include policy id and signal snapshot.

2025-03-03 — SRE: Ran chaos test in staging: injected 5xx spike into cohort B at 40% traffic; attenuation engine paused ramp at 50% and reversed to 20% as expected. Follow-up: add hysteresis to prevent thrash.

2025-03-05 — Security: Initial threat model completed; recommended adding signed policy blobs and HMAC verification when control plane reads policy from git. Also recommended KMS-backed audit log encryption.
notes: Design decisions: use exponential decay curve by default (configurable), allow per-tenant overrides for enterprise customers, and do not auto-rollout to LTS channel without explicit opt-in.
Open questions: how to incorporate model output-quality regressions measured by synthetic evals into the fast signal loop without creating feedback loops?
Follow-ups: add fine-grained per-route attenuation (text-generation vs embeddings) in a follow-up ticket; consider ML-driven ramp pacing in Q3.

Runbook excerpt: if attenuation pauses ramp, notify on-call, capture snapshot of last 2 minutes of telemetry, and attempt automated rollback if two independent signals exceed thresholds for >3 minutes.
